rounds.proof_sketch: Original loop: i∈[0,3], each thread covers 4 consecutive positions. Mutated: i∈[0,4], each thread covers 5 positions, creating overlap at position idx+4 between consecutive threads. Both threads write hardtanh(input[idx+4]), which is deterministic → identical values written. Guard 'if (pos < size)' prevents OOB access. All 262144 positions receive correct hardtanh output in both versions.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation extends the loop from 4 to 5 iterations, causing threads to write overlapping elements. Specifically, thread N writes position (N+1)*4, which thread N+1 also writes. However, since both threads read the same input value and apply the identical hardtanh transformation, they produce and write the same output value. This write-write race is benign. The boundary guard 'if (pos < size)' prevents any out-of-bounds access. Every element in the output tensor receives exactly the correct hardtanh value regardless of which thread writes it, making the outputs bitwise identical.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable — the mutation creates benign redundant writes that produce identical output values. No input value pattern can expose a difference because the mathematical operation performed on each output position is unchanged.
rounds.recommendations: When testing vectorized kernels with loop bound mutations, verify not just coverage but also write-collision semantics. Mutations creating overlapping writes may be equivalent if the transformation is deterministic and idempotent for same-value overwrites. Consider adding assertions or atomic operations in debug builds to detect unintended thread overlap patterns.
